text:
sanjay: heads up — recurrent ECC + Xid spikes from rack42 over ~36h. opening thread for short RCA notes and next steps.

infra-bot: [ALERT] rack42: ECC error rate 12.3x baseline, Xid32/Xid43 bursts at 2026-03-15T03:02Z..2026-03-16T15:18Z

sanjay: quick snapshot from host rack42-node05 (nv-smi + dmesg snippets below). noticed spikes align with short PDU voltage dips in the same window.

sanjay: ```
# nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0: serial=SNXK-2307-0045 ECC errors (volatile): 0
GPU 1: serial=SNXK-2307-0046 ECC errors (volatile): 1042
GPU 2: serial=SNXK-2307-0047 ECC errors (volatile): 998
GPU 3: serial=SNXK-2307-0048 ECC errors (volatile): 1120

# dmesg | tail -n 8
[Mar15 03:02:11] NVRM: Xid (32): PID 1123: GPF, PID 1123, Reason 0x0000000a
[Mar15 03:02:11] NVRM: Xid (43): GPU cluster reset request
[Mar16 14:59:27] NVRM: Xid (32): PID 4521: CE single-bit ECC error detected
```

lia: thanks. can you paste the PDU/ups history for the same interval? if voltage sag overlaps that's a strong lead.

sanjay: PDU logs attached (excerpt):

```
2026-03-15T03:02:10Z rack42-pdu2: voltage=197VAC, drop_duration=1.8s
2026-03-15T03:02:12Z rack42-pdu2: voltage=230VAC, restored
2026-03-16T14:59:25Z rack42-pdu1: voltage=188VAC, drop_duration=2.1s
```

ev an: (evan) odd — both short sag events coincide with highest ECC/Xid counts. contents look like sub-2s dips, not full power loss. can those cause GPU micro-resets?

ben: yep, GPUs are sensitive to brownouts. we've seen single-bit ECC spikes when VRMs hiccup. also want to check BIOS/flexboot changes — any BIOS pushes lately?

maya: ops-oncall, did we push any firmware/BIOS/driver updates to rack42 in the last 7 days?

ops-oncall: no mass BIOS flip. did an emergency kernel bump on 2026-03-14 on a subset of hosts for security patch (linux 6.2.19 -> 6.2.21) but not targeted to rack42 nodes.

lia: serial prefix for hot GPUs is SNXK-2307 (looks like vendor lot SYN-2307). do we have inventory window for that lot?

sanjay: inventory shows SNXK-2307 cards installed 2026-01-10..2026-01-17 across racks 38-43. failure concentration is currently only rack42 (8/8 nodes with >600 ECC events each). others show negligible ECC.

ben: that points to a rack-local factor (power distribution / PDUs / bus / cable) rather than purely batch failure. but the lot may be more fragile under power noise.

evan: quick hypothesis list: 1) transient PDU voltage sags -> GPU VRM instability -> ECC/Xid spike, 2) PSU/PDU feed imbalance on rack42 causing microfluctuations, 3) firmware/driver not main cause but makes cards less forgiving.

maya: proposed immediate mitigation:
- cordon/drain affected nodes (rack42-node01..08) from prod now
- switch critical workloads to spare capacity (preemptible pool)
- schedule vendor RMA for serials SNXK-2307-0045..0048 (and nearby serials in the same chassis)
- increase ECC scrub frequency and enable `nv_gpu_reset_on_xid=0` (temporary)
- open PD alert with infra building team to replace/inspect PDU2 and PDU1 breakers

lia: +1 on drain. add temporary capacity limit to avoid auto-eviction churn. also let's snapshot kernel logs across all nodes for cross-correlation.

ops-oncall: I've started draining rack42-node01..08 (evacuate jobs). ETA finish 20m. marking nodes `quarantine:power_swing` in fleet metadata.

ben: action items and owners:
- sanjay: collect full PDU time-series and attach to incident ticket (ETA 2h)
- lia: run nvlink/power integrity tests after drain and report (ETA 4h)
- maya: open vendor RMA + include serials, test vectors, PDU logs (ETA 6h)
- evan: coordinate capacity shuffles and set autoscaler hold (ETA 30m)
- ops-oncall: confirm hardware vendor on-site inspection request and schedule (ETA EOD)

sanjay: longer-term notes: if vendor confirms sensitivity of lot to voltage noise, consider avoiding SYN-2307 in >2U dense racks or require PDU firmware that offers active smoothing. also add a quick PDU-voltage correlation alert to fleet metrics so we catch <3s sags earlier.

lia: also suggest adding a small burn-in on replacements with power-stability stress test (pdu-induced micro-sag sim) before returning to prod.

maya: agreed. I'll add that to the postmortem doc and draft recommended SRE runbook changes.

ben: tagging for postmortem: root cause = power-swing induced VRM instability exposing sensitive vendor lot; contributing = lack of existing <3s voltage-sag alert and insufficient pre-prod power-stability burn-in.

sanjay: ok will summarize and paste into the incident tracker. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
